evidence: Clear directory structure with logical separation of concerns: 'model/', 'operations/', 'utils/', 'errors/'
Domain models (Dataset, Database, Datatable, Data, PointInTime) implemented as classes with behavior (not just DTOs)
Operations layer (GetOperation, ListOperation) reused by models via inheritance, promoting DRY
Dependency flow: high-level domain classes (e.g., Dataset) depend on lower-level utilities/connection, but packages are organized by domain capability rather than technical layering
Minimal cross-boundary coupling; each module (e.g., model, operations) has cohesive responsibilities
No explicit messaging infrastructure, service discovery, or deployment boundaries typical of microservices
Single package namespace (nasdaqdatalink) used throughout—no service boundaries or process isolation
Inheritance used heavily for operation reuse (e.g., Dataset inherits GetOperation, ListOperation)
Tests organized in parallel structure to source, reflecting modular cohesion
risks: Some classes (e.g., Dataset, Datatable) contain both data and behavior across multiple responsibilities (data access + business logic)
Heavy use of inheritance (e.g., multiple inheritance in Data class) may reduce flexibility and increase coupling
Tight coupling between model and operations layer could hinder future decoupling or replacement of access patterns
